name: II
editorial_article: 'II', released on August 30, 1994, is the blockbuster second studio album by the Philadelphia vocal group Boyz II Men. Following the immense success of their debut, 'Cooleyhighharmony', the quartet set out to cement their place as the dominant force in 1990s R&B. The album was meticulously crafted to maintain their commercial stranglehold, with the members actively studying sales trends and Motown utilizing market research to curate a collection of polished, high-fidelity soul ballads. Shawn Stockman, a member of the group, later explained that the title was intended to signify a direct continuation of their first project, functioning like a cinematic sequel.\n\nThe album's production credits represent a "who's who" of the mid-90s R&B landscape, featuring contributions from industry titans such as Babyface, Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, Dallas Austin, and L.A. Reid, alongside rising production duo Tim & Bob. The resulting sound was a masterful blend of the group's signature vocal harmonies and contemporary hip-hop-influenced R&B production. 'II' was a massive commercial juggernaut, achieving diamond status and becoming one of the best-selling R&B albums of all time. It produced two consecutive Billboard Hot 100 number-one hits, "I'll Make Love to You" and "On Bended Knee," the latter of which famously replaced the former at the top spot—a rare chart feat that solidified the group's historic status. Beyond its commercial impact, 'II' was critically recognized, winning the inaugural Grammy Award for Best R&B Album in 1995. Its legacy remains as a definitive artifact of the mid-90s R&B golden era, showcasing a group at the height of their technical and popular powers.
